title: Georgia football commit Marcellus Young Casario dies after ‘medical incident’
content:
Marcellus Young Casario, a Canadian high school football player who had committed to play for Georgia, died Friday after what his high school called a medical incident.

Casario, a native of Halifax, Nova Scotia, was a senior defensive lineman at Rabun Gap-Nacoochee School, a boarding school in northeast Georgia.

The school announced Friday that a boarding student died, and the football team’s playoff game that night was postponed. A school spokesman confirmed Saturday that the student was Casario. No other immediate details were provided.

“The boarding student had a medical incident this morning,” the school statement from Friday read. “Rabun Gap immediately followed our emergency response protocols, and local emergency personnel responded, transferring the student to the hospital.”

Casario moved from Nova Scotia to Rabun Gap two years ago, seeking more visibility for a college football scholarship. Georgia eventually offered a scholarship, and Casario committed in June. The 247Sports Composite ranked him as a three-star prospect.
